name: 02-networks
title: The five networks
description: Define, start and autostart the five libvirt networks of the ebook's fixed lab plan on the physical host: NAT-ed lab-mgmt (10.100.99.1/24), isolated lab-storage-fe (10.200.99.1/24, MTU 9000), isolated lab-storage-be (10.201.99.1/24, MTU 9000), the VLAN-unaware lab-guest trunk, and NAT-ed lab-public (203.0.113.1/28) — then prove the bridges are up and the storage pair really carries MTU 9000.
source: Generated from runbooks/lab/lab-networks.yaml in the MatrixClaw lab repository. That runbook built this phase of the real 32 GB estate on 20-21 July 2026; the run records hold every command's exit code and output.
honesty: Steps change this machine and are gated. Each carries an 'already' probe, so a re-run skips what is done rather than repeating it. Checks are read-only and carry exact-match markers so they cannot pass on their own error text.

steps.title: Net lab mgmt
steps.run:
cat > /tmp/lab-mgmt.xml << 'EOF'
<network>
  <name>lab-mgmt</name>
  <bridge name='br-lab-mgmt'/>
  <forward mode='nat'/>
  <ip address='10.100.99.1' netmask='255.255.255.0'/>
</network>
EOF
export LIBVIRT_DEFAULT_URI=qemu:///system
virsh net-define /tmp/lab-mgmt.xml
virsh net-start lab-mgmt
virsh net-autostart lab-mgmt
rm -f /tmp/lab-mgmt.xml

steps.title: Net lab storage fe
steps.run:
cat > /tmp/lab-storage-fe.xml << 'EOF'
<network>
  <name>lab-storage-fe</name>
  <bridge name='br-lab-stgfe'/>
  <mtu size='9000'/>
  <ip address='10.200.99.1' netmask='255.255.255.0'/>
</network>
EOF
export LIBVIRT_DEFAULT_URI=qemu:///system
virsh net-define /tmp/lab-storage-fe.xml

checks.title: Five networks active
checks.run: export LIBVIRT_DEFAULT_URI=qemu:///system; for n in lab-mgmt lab-storage-fe lab-storage-be lab-guest lab-public; do virsh net-list | grep -q "$n .*active" || exit 1; done && echo FIVE-NETWORKS-ACTIVE

checks.title: Five bridges up
checks.run: test "$(ip -br link | grep -c br-lab)" -eq 5 && echo FIVE-BRIDGES-OK
